summary: The interface ioctls by which a program reads and changes the machine's network configuration, on the rtl8139, and two cards in one machine, each case a boot of its own that tests/cases/machine/netif_scenario.c drives

cases.behavior: netifprobe passes each row at the debug shell of a machine with QEMU's address on the rtl8139: the interface ioctls, a change of address that aborts the connections open across it, the interface taken down, which drops the datagram the host sends, and brought up, which receives the next, and the routes

steps.does: boot the test image to the debug shell

run netifprobe at the debug shell, send it a datagram from the host with hostpeer send through the forward when it prints NETIFPROBE DOWN and again when it prints NETIFPROBE UP, and take its report from the console

assertions.checks: the raw descriptor that BusyBox's DHCP client asks the interface through, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW and IPPROTO_RAW, opens
a raw socket for TCP, a protocol the stack does not carry, answers EPROTONOSUPPORT
eth0 has index 1, and SIOCGIFINDEX of eth9 answers ENODEV
SIOCGIFNAME of index 1 gives eth0, and of index 7 answers ENODEV
SIOCGIFHWADDR of eth0 gives an Ethernet address that is not all zeros
SIOCGIFADDR of eth0 reads its address
the address is 10.0.2.15, the one QEMU's user network gives
the netmask reads back as 255.255.255.0
the broadcast address is the subnet's, 10.0.2.255
the MTU is 1500
the flags have IFF_UP or IFF_BROADCAST, IFF_MULTICAST and IFF_RUNNING
the query descriptor refuses bind, connect, listen, read and write with EOPNOTSUPP, and a poll of it reports POLLERR at once
a TCP connection to the machine's own 10.0.2.15 at port 7400 opens and is accepted, to be held across the change of address
a child at uid 1000 that sets the address is answered EPERM
the address 192.168.90.20 and the mask 255.255.255.0 are set, and the address reads back
after the change a write to one end of the held connection and a read of the other answer ENETRESET, and SO_ERROR then reads 0
the listener accepts a second connection, to the new address
the same address and mask set again leave the second connection's SO_ERROR 0
the address 172.16.1.2 set alone takes the classful mask 255.255.0.0
that later change leaves the first connection's SO_ERROR 0, and 192.168.90.20/24 is set again
with 10.0.2.15/24 set again the gateway answers a ping, and a datagram socket binds port 9999
eth0 taken down with SIOCSIFFLAGS reads neither IFF_UP nor IFF_RUNNING
the gateway does not answer a ping while eth0 is down
the datagram the host sends after NETIFPROBE DOWN raises eth0's receive drops in /proc/net/dev, and the socket receives nothing
with eth0 brought back up the gateway answers a ping
a nonblocking read of the second connection, open across the change back to 10.0.2.15, answers ENETRESET
the datagram the host sends after NETIFPROBE UP reaches the socket
with 192.168.90.20/24 set again, the addresses 0.1.2.3, 240.1.2.3 and 224.0.0.1 answer EINVAL
a default route through 192.168.90.1 is taken
a default route through 10.0.2.2, off the subnet, answers ENETUNREACH
a route to 10.10.10.0/24 is added and removed
a default route with no gateway answers EINVAL and keeps the gateway, whose removal then succeeds
a route added or removed for eth9 answers ENODEV
the route to the machine's own subnet is added, and its removal answers EOPNOTSUPP
the default route is removed
a second removal of the default route answers ESRCH
192.168.1.0 is accepted and not in force until the mask 255.255.0.0 makes it a host, and then the mask 255.255.255.0 answers EINVAL
192.168.1.0 set on a machine with no address, refused the mask 255.255.255.0, leaves the machine with no address
10.0.2.15/24 and the default route through 10.0.2.2 are set again, and the gateway answers a ping

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the probe changes the machine's address, flags and routes and takes its interface down, which would cut a running machine off from its network, and the host sends its datagrams through the forward of QEMU's user network; tests/native/probes.cases runs the probe's queries natively

cases.behavior: netifprobe configures a machine booted with rach2.ip=none on the rtl8139 from nothing: an address, then a mask, then a default route, after which the gateway answers

steps.does: boot the test image with rach2.ip=none to the debug shell
run netifprobe at the debug shell and take its report from the console

assertions.checks: the raw descriptor that BusyBox's DHCP client asks the interface through, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW and IPPROTO_RAW, opens
a raw socket for TCP, a protocol the stack does not carry, answers EPROTONOSUPPORT
eth0 has index 1, and SIOCGIFINDEX of eth9 answers ENODEV
SIOCGIFNAME of index 1 gives eth0, and of index 7 answers ENODEV
SIOCGIFHWADDR of eth0 gives an Ethernet address that is not all zeros
SIOCGIFADDR of eth0 reads its address
a machine with no address reports the netmask 0
the address 10.0.2.15 is set on the machine that has none
the address set alone takes the classful mask 255.0.0.0

native.reason: the machine boots with rach2.ip=none, and the probe configures its one interface from nothing

cases.behavior: two e1000s on two networks are two interfaces, each with its own station address and address, the second's given by rach2.ifaddr, and pingtest and `netifprobe second` pass

steps.does: boot the test image with two e1000s to the debug shell
run pingtest at the debug shell and take its report from the console
run `netifprobe second` at the debug shell and take its report from the console
find the two cards' lines in the boot log, read from the console up to the end of the last report

assertions.checks: three pings to the gateway each get a reply
a ping to an address nobody answers fails
the child writes its byte just before its ping, and /proc shows it asleep in the call
while the child is in its call, the parent's ping of the loopback address answers EBUSY
the parent's clock readings while the child waits span some time, so the wait sleeps
the child reports the length of its call through the pipe
the child is reaped and exited normally
the child's ping returned ETIMEDOUT
the child's call lasted at least 3990 ms, four seconds of the kernel's ticks
after the reap the parent's loopback ping returns a round-trip time of 0 or more
a data ping of 65508 bytes, and on x86-64 one of a size past 32 bits, is refused with EMSGSIZE
the raw descriptor that the interfaces are asked through, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW and IPPROTO_RAW, opens
each card's gateway, 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.3.2, answers a ping
eth1 is up, and taken down with SIOCSIFFLAGS reads neither IFF_UP nor IFF_RUNNING
eth0 stays up, and the gateway 10.0.2.2 still answers a ping
the netlink link dump reports eth1 neither up nor running and eth0 up and running
eth1 is brought back up, and the link dump reports it up
/proc/net/dev names eth0 and eth1
SO_BINDTODEVICE takes eth1 and reads it back, answers ENODEV for eth9 and keeps eth1, and clears with an empty name
accept on a stream socket that never listened and on a datagram socket answers EINVAL
both ends of a TCP connection to 10.0.3.5 have that address, and accept on either answers EINVAL
getsockname of a packet socket bound to no interface reports none and no hardware address, and of those bound to eth0 and eth1 the interface and its card's Ethernet address
an ARP request for 10.0.3.2 sent through the packet socket bound to eth1 is answered on eth1, over Ethernet, to this machine or to everyone
the packet socket bound to eth0 is given nothing that arrived on another interface
the boot log has `net: eth0: e1000`: the first card became eth0
the boot log has `net: eth1: e1000`: the second card became eth1
the station addresses of the lines `net: eth0: e1000, station` and `net: eth1: e1000, station` differ
the boot log has `net: eth1: configured by its station address`
the boot log has `net: eth1: IPv4 10.0.3.5/24, gateway 10.0.3.2`, which rach2.ifaddr gives the second card's station address
the boot log has `net: eth0: IPv4 10.0.2.15/24`: the first card kept its own address

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the machine has two e1000s, each on a user network of QEMU's, and an address given on the boot line
